text:
maria: onboarding a new HF model (hf-user/whispery-13b) — seeing tokencount blow up on chat inputs. Suspect a weird normalizer + zero-width character interaction. Anyone seen this?
anand: yep, ran into similar with another HF import. What's the diff vs our Redwood pretokenizer?
maria: quick repro: input = 'Hi‍there' (ZWJ between words). HF tokenizer (pretrained) => 9 tokens. Redwood-converted tokenizer => 3 tokens. But when we run NFKC normalize before byte-fallback it goes back to 9. Means ordering matters.
li: can you paste the serializer config from the converted tokenizer?
maria: paste: ```json
{"normalizer": [{"type":"NFKC"},{"type":"strip"}], "pre_tokenizer":{"type":"byte_fallback_or_whitespace"}}
```
li: ah, we put NFKC first in conversion. HF model's original had a custom normalizer that preserves ZERO WIDTH JOINER. We applied generic NFKC which collapses joiner sequences in some scripts.
evan: interesting — also saw chat template leading spaces getting dropped if pretokenizer treats ZWJ as whitespace. That breaks role detection ("User: ‍Hi" becomes "User:Hi").
manad: (typo in my handle, ignore)
ci-bot: conversion-checker: tokenizer config missing "added_tokens" mapping for special chat markers like "<|system|>" — flagged.
anand: two quick experiments: 1) change normalizer order to apply byte-fallback before NFKC, 2) add explicit mapping that replaces ‌/‍ with � only if byte-fallback needed. Results?
maria: 1) gave consistent token counts with HF in 85% of cases but still misaligned on combining marks. 2) mapping -> keeps tokencount stable but changes model behavior on some test prompts (punctuation spacing differences).
li: can we add a small preflight that checks for any non-visible codepoints in prompts and warns customers? e.g., detect category Cf characters and log example tokens.
evan: here's a tiny script I used: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
import unicodedata
t = Tokenizer.from_file('converted.json')
def has_invis(s):
    return [c for c in s if unicodedata.category(c)=='Cf']
print(has_invis('User:‍Hello'))
print(t.encode('User:‍Hello').tokens)
```
maria: solid. Filing evals: added new prompt-suite with ZWJ/ZWNJ/zero-width-space + combining marks across languages. Early fail cases: Hindi devanagari combining sequences, Arabic diacritics, emoji zwj sequences.
anand: for rollout plan: 1) revert conversion to preserve HF normalizer exactly where present, 2) add conversion test that diffs token counts for 200 curated prompts, 3) expose a flag on Redwood Private to enforce legacy-vs-strict normalization.
li: +1. Also add docs note under model bring-up checklist: "inspect tokenizer.normalizer in HF config.json; avoid blind NFKC when model training preserved ZWJ semantics"
evan: I'll open a quick PR with a convert option `--preserve-zero-width` and add that preflight.
ci-bot: PR #2847 opened by evan: "preserve zero-width in tokenizer conversion", auto-run tests queued.
maria: thanks. Once CI passes, we'll run quantized evals (int8/qlora) to check any quality drift from normalization changes. If anyone has small prompt sets with expected token-level outputs, drop them here. :seedling:
